title: Same heat, different rise
hook: Give water and iron the same heat. Do they warm the same?

knows: that heating something raises its temperature
kilojoules as a unit of energy
doesNotKnow: that different materials need different energy per degree (specific heat)

misconception: The same heat warms every material equally.
objective: The learner can explain that 4.2 kJ warms 1 kg of water by about 1.0 °C but 1 kg of iron by about 9.4 °C, because water needs about 4.18 kJ per kg per degree and iron only about 0.449, and that this is why seas change temperature slowly.

claims.text: Water needs about 4.18 kJ to warm 1 kg by 1 °C.
claims.source: Specific heat capacity of liquid water at 25 °C, 4.18 kJ/(kg K) (CRC Handbook, 'Properties of water').

claims.text: Iron needs only about 0.449 kJ to warm 1 kg by 1 °C.
claims.source: Specific heat of iron at 25 °C, 0.449 J/(g K) (CRC Handbook, 'Heat capacity of the elements at 25 °C').

claims.text: 4.2 kJ warms 1 kg of water by about 1.0 °C and 1 kg of iron by about 9.4 °C, about 9 times as much.
claims.source: ΔT = Q/(m c): 4.2/4.18 = 1.00 K; 4.2/0.449 = 9.35 K; ratio 9.31. Node script; Demo.tsx computes TIMES from the same constants.

claims.text: Few common substances soak up as much energy per degree as water, which is why seas and lakes warm and cool slowly.
claims.source: Water's specific heat is among the highest of common liquids and solids (CRC Handbook tables; Atkins & Jones, Chemical Principles, on hydrogen bonding and heat capacity). Climate moderation by oceans: NOAA ocean heat content resources; standard physical geography texts.

claims.text: Stage: the model assumes no heat is lost and constant specific heats over the range.
claims.source: Demo.tsx, ΔT = Q/(m c) with fixed c.

recall.question: A 1 kg iron pan and 1 kg of water sit on equal burners for the same time. Which is hotter after a minute?
recall.why: Iron needs about 9 times less energy per kilogram per degree, so the same heat raises it about 9 times as much.
